effects.note: The soldered brass collar is worn around the swineherd’s neck.
The ram’s horn hangs at his belt.
The Sheffield knife hangs at his belt.
The silver collar identifies the jester’s servitude.
The jester carries a sword made of lath.
Gurth picks up the quarterstaff before setting out.
Aymer stakes his own collar in the wager. No delivery to Brian occurs.
The Palmer takes the ivory reliquary from his bosom and offers it as a pledge.
Brian removes the gold chain and flings it on the board as his pledge.
Aymer delivers the reliquary to Brother Ambrose.
Aymer puts the pledged chain in his own perfumed-leather pouch.
The entering Palmer carries the iron-shod staff with a palm branch at its upper end.
Isaac writes the Hebrew order on his cap and delivers it to the Pilgrim. The promised choice of horse and armour is not yet a completed delivery.
The anonymous challenger enters the lists riding a gallant black horse and salutes the prince and ladies with his lance.
The entering challenger wears steel armour richly inlaid with gold. No intervening delivery is narrated, and the rider’s concealed name is not disclosed here.
The tournament victor receives the awarded horse, distinct from his borrowed equipment.
Gurth accepts ten gold pieces as a personal reward, separately from his master’s money.
The master entrusts the payment bag to Gurth, who takes it beneath his cloak and departs.

effects.reportText: Gurth reports that the borrowed horse has been restored to Isaac’s stable. The former rider is absent, and neither the return journey nor a current person holding its reins is shown.
effects.note: Gurth reports that the steed has been restored to Isaac’s stable; Isaac is not thereby shown physically holding its reins.

effects.reportText: Gurth discusses the price of his absent master’s supplied armour. Its current whereabouts and a handoff are not shown; the report of the horse’s return does not establish a return of the armour.
effects.note: Gurth asks the price of the supplied armour. Its return is not stated, unlike the horse’s return to the stable. Current whereabouts remain unestablished by this conversation.
Gurth counts eighty zecchins onto the table for Isaac. The remaining bag stays with him; its total original sum was not stated.
Isaac gives the receipt for horse and armour; Gurth folds it under his cap.
Rebecca gives the silk purse containing a hundred gold pieces: eighty for the master and the remainder for his attendant. The amounts are allocations within the purse, not duplicated piles of coins.
The masked captain takes the large leather pouch from Gurth’s breast.
Rebecca’s silk purse is enclosed within the seized leather pouch.
The personal coins are not separately located during seizure of the larger pouch; do not assume an unreported second purse remains securely with Gurth.
Gurth nearly recovers the pouch after striking the captain, but the thieves secure it again. His attempted recovery does not restore custody.
The silk purse remains with the recaptured bag; Gurth’s dash has failed.
The robbers pronounce Gurth and his purse safe and release him with guides. Restoration is implied by his intact release; no separate hand-to-hand return is described.
The treasure is spared and accompanies the released attendant. The precise return handoff is not separately narrated.
The release preserves Gurth’s personal money as well as his master’s trust; the intervening separation of the coin lots is not shown.
The anonymous black-armoured rider has a strong black horse. No future ambush injury is disclosed.

evidence.title: The axe turned against its owner

effects.note: The rescuer wrenches the axe from Athelstane and strikes him with it. Its subsequent disposal is not narrated here.
The narrator discloses that the rescuer’s sword broke against Front-de-Boeuf. The fragments’ whereabouts are not stated.
John throws down the warder to stop the encounter. The exact point where it lands is not supplied.
Rowena places the chaplet on the unhelmeted victor’s head. The spoken identification of Ivanhoe is later; this award does not reveal that name early.
An attendant puts the sealed foreign billet into Prince John’s hand.
John puts the billet into Fitzurse’s and De Bracy’s hands successively; De Bracy is the last named recipient.
John awards the bugle to the successful archer; Locksley gives the money prize to Hubert rather than joining John’s service.
Wamba takes a real sword from an attendant, fights, and escapes into the thicket.
Locksley unbuckles the horn and baldric and gives them to Wamba.
The shoulder belt is handed over with the horn; no identity with an earlier unspecified silver baldric is assumed.
Locksley removes the feather from his cap and gives it to Wamba.
Locksley draws a vizard from his pouch before reconnoitring.
The hermit locks the door and deposits the key beneath the threshold, rather than carrying it away.
After Front-de-Boeuf and De Bracy handle the demand, Brian takes and reads it.
The folded reply passes from its writer through an unnamed squire to the unnamed yeoman waiting outside. Neither messenger is identified as an existing named attendant.
The hermit passes the reply to Gurth, who passes it to Wamba; Wamba gives it to Locksley.
The Black Knight takes the reply from Locksley and translates it for the company.
Wamba is now muffled in the borrowed clerical disguise, beyond the earlier proposal to put it on.
The borrowed hood conceals the disguised jester.
At the castle portal Wamba wears the hermit’s knotted cord twisted around his middle. This directly established possession precedes the proposed exchange with Cedric.
The exchange of dress is now accomplished; this is later than the proposed exchange.
Cedric takes the clerical disguise.
The cord is included in the completed exchange of dress.
Wamba takes Cedric’s cloak in exchange for the friar’s clothes.
Wamba takes Cedric’s girdle as part of the exchange.
Front-de-Boeuf entrusts the dispatch to the disguised Cedric. His intended delivery to Malvoisin is not a completed delivery.
Athelstane throws down his glove. The subsequent instruction to hang it on antlers is an order, not evidence of a completed placement.
In the retrospective account of her treatment, Rebecca applies the medicine and refuses to entrust the phial to another physician. This is not a fresh injury at the present siege.
De Bracy picks up his sword and gives it to Locksley at the barbican. Later release does not itself restore the weapon.
Ulrica brandishes the distaff from the burning turret.
The turret falls with Ulrica. No recovery of the distaff is narrated, and it is not assigned to a rescuer.

Cedric declares Gurth free. Gurth then calls for a smith and file to remove the collar; the actual cutting is not narrated. Its presence in the last-known inventory no longer denotes continuing servitude.

effects.reportText: Locksley has the horn and baldric again and gives them to the Black Knight.
effects.note: Locksley has the horn again by paragraph53, without a narrated return from Wamba. The Black Knight accepts the offered gift and blows it at56.

effects.reportText: Locksley has the horn and baldric again and gives them to the Black Knight.
effects.note: The rich baldric accompanies the gifted horn; the earlier return to Locksley was not shown.
Isaac supplies his tablets; Aymer writes and seals the appeal, then returns them to Isaac. The writing interlude does not leave them with Aymer.
Conrade first takes the tablets from Isaac for Beaumanoir, who opens and reads them; Conrade then explicitly takes the letter from his superior to read aloud.

effects.reportText: Aymer’s postscript says that Brian’s pledge-chain is now around an unnamed outlaw deer-stalker’s neck.
effects.note: Aymer’s postscript reports the chain now around an unnamed outlaw deer-stalker’s neck. Its recipient is not identified as Locksley or the hermit.
A small scrap is thrust into Rebecca’s hand as she passes through the hall. Its sender and contents are not yet disclosed.
The witness produces his small medicine box and the Grand Master takes it. This old gift is distinct from Rebecca’s retained phial.
Rebecca reads the advice to demand a champion and destroys the scrap. A later admission about its sender does not recreate it.
Rebecca throws the embroidered glove down before the Grand Master as her gage.
The Grand Master calls for the glove and looks at it; possession is now established.
Albert is explicitly still holding the glove and later conceals it in his mantle. He never actually hands it to Brian in this exchange.
Higg takes Rebecca’s Hebrew scroll for delivery to Isaac.
Higg offers the scroll and Isaac glances at it before falling insensible. The text does not specify whose hand retains it through his collapse.
Ivanhoe mounts the Prior’s jennet before leaving Saint Botolph’s. A later unidentified exhausted horse is not automatically identified as Malkin.
Wamba is now explicitly described carrying a target with his cutting falchion; the narrator also reports his earlier use during the storming.
The narrator explicitly says that Wamba’s real falchion has replaced the wooden sword. The wooden blade’s location is not given.
The Black Knight unclasps the baldric and Wamba hangs the bugle around his own neck.
The belt passes with the bugle; Wamba later delays returning it and blows the alarm himself.
The attacker wounds the charger mortally and it falls. The rider is not thereby mortally wounded, and this horse is no longer a usable mount.
Gurth is shown riding his master’s war-horse. The intervening handoff is not narrated.
Athelstane recounts using the key from the sacristan’s belt to release his shackles. He does not say he carried it away, so no present inventory acquisition is inferred.
Brian names the horse he is riding while proposing escape. The claimed past victory over its former owner is reported history, not a new acquisition.
Albert lays the glove at the Grand Master’s feet. Acceptance of the pledge does not put it in Brian’s hands.
The Grand Master holds Rebecca’s glove and throws it into the lists to begin the encounter.
Rebecca offers a casket. Its contents have not yet been revealed, and the offer alone is not a completed transfer.
Rowena opens the silver-chased casket. She tenders it back in protest, but Rebecca urges her to keep it; no completed return or separately spoken acceptance is narrated.
The opened casket reveals a diamond necklace, first disclosed here rather than at the preceding offer.
The matching diamond ear-jewels are disclosed with the necklace when the casket is opened.

scope: Source-reviewed last-known custody for the55 selected objects and mounts; unshown transfers and whereabouts remain unasserted. Application and final release evidence are recorded separately.
limitations: Custody is the last source record, not an invented disposal or unshown handoff.
The55-object selection and uncertain outcomes are documented in INVENTORY_REVIEW.md.
Absent former-holder states must not be fabricated as physical presence.
